prediction.reason: engineering mechanism candidate; no target latency prediction

score.reason: cross-instance visibility and persistence error oracle; no native timing truth opened

result: page/detail now reload the current persisted catalog before serving reads, so a long-lived instance observes creates, updates, and deletions made by another instance. Invalid persisted JSON remains an explicit read failure rather than a successful stale response. The separately registered update/delete contention hypothesis was tested and deferred because the existing lock-held reload path is linearizable for the tested races.
limitations: The evidence covers same-host multiple instances/processes and HTTP servers, not a distributed filesystem consistency guarantee
Read refresh reparses the small catalog on every page/detail call; no throughput optimization was attempted
HTTP persistence errors currently use the existing generic 422 exception path and may deserve a dedicated catalog error code
No native accuracy, latency, or deployment claim
